ATTACHED REFERENCE: the ONE attached image is our own GRUNT GOBLIN sprite sheet from this same game, drawn for it from a text-only brief: match its pixel-art style EXACTLY (the same art-pixel size, the same near-black outline, the same muted night palette and flat shading). Never copy the grunt itself: the character below is a new, original one. The look in words: classic chunky retro pixel art for the enemy sprites of a modern retro first-person horde shooter set on a cold moonlit night: bold, instantly readable silhouettes with big heads and expressive faces; every material shaded with 2 to 3 flat tones (a lighter tone on the upper front, a mid tone, a dark shadow tone), lit softly from the upper front; small clusters of darker pixels as texture on skin, cloth and wood; thin dark interior lines for folds, muscles and planks; a muted, slightly desaturated palette (olive, ochre-grey, dull brown, slate, dull iron) in which only fire and glowing eyes are bright. Everything below is an original design.

STYLE: a 2D PIXEL-ART SPRITE SHEET for a video game. True low-resolution pixel art: each figure is about 46 art pixels tall and every art pixel is a crisp square block of the same size, hard edges, NO anti-aliasing, NO gradients, NO soft airbrush shading, NO blur, NO noise texture; a limited muted palette (about 12 to 16 flat colours for the character); a clean 1 to 2 art-pixel near-black outline (#1a1418) around every figure. All figures face the viewer (front view, flying toward the camera), drawn at the same scale in every frame.
BACKGROUND: one flat, perfectly uniform, solid pure magenta #FF00FF everywhere behind and between the figures. No ground, no floor line, no cast shadow, no text, no labels, no numbers, no frame borders, no grid lines.

THE CHARACTER, BAT GREMLIN (a flying goblin): a small olive-green goblin (#6f7a3a skin) with big sideways ears and goggles pushed up on its forehead, STRAPPED with leather belts UNDER a home-made GLIDER of two big stitched BAT WINGS (dark brown-grey leather patches sewn together with pale stitches, stretched over thin wooden ribs, ragged scalloped edges), its legs dangling below. The wings are very wide (about three times the goblin's width). Muted olive, dark leather brown-grey, pale stitches, dull wood.

LAYOUT: exactly 11 figures of the SAME character in 3 horizontal rows, read left to right:
Row 1 (top, 4 figures) FLYING, wing flap cycle: (1) wings fully raised up in a V; (2) wings level, spread wide; (3) wings swept down; (4) wings level again, legs swinging.
Row 2 (middle, 4 figures): (5) DIVE: wings folded back tight, body pointing down toward the viewer, mouth open screaming, claws out; (6) DIVE: the same, steeper, wings tucked; (7) BURNING: the wings ON FIRE, orange-yellow pixel flames on the wings and its back, the goblin screaming; (8) BURNING: another flailing pose, a wing torn and burning.
Row 3 (bottom, 3 figures) DEATH, a tumbling fall: (9) hit, the glider crumpling, spinning sideways; (10) falling upside down, wings broken; (11) crashed on the ground as a low heap of torn wings and goblin.
Every figure stands alone with wide magenta gaps; nothing touches or overlaps.
